text.ka479d909: Afghanistan is a landlocked, mountainous country at the crossroads of Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent. Since 2021, the Taliban's Islamic Emirate has governed the country with forces drawn from the insurgency. Part of the equipment left behind by the former Afghan army remains in service. Its forces have clashed with Pakistan since 2025.
text.kb3b4b940: Light infantry forces with poorly maintained equipment inherited from the former Afghan army. Guerrilla and internal control doctrine.
text.ka522be51: Angola lies on the Atlantic in southern Africa and draws most of its revenue from oil. Its army, shaped by the long civil war, fields plentiful but ageing Soviet equipment. Its forces have fought in the conflicts of the Great Lakes region and remain among the largest in southern Africa.
text.k95909a62: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin (Su-30K, T-72, BMP). Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k95097465: Albania lies on the Adriatic and Ionian Seas opposite Italy. A NATO member since 2009, it has small armed forces and hosts a renovated allied air base at Kuçova. Its coastline partly controls the Strait of Otranto, the entrance to the Adriatic.
text.k7bee2f2b: Light forces equipped with Western materiel and Turkish drones. Collective defense doctrine.
text.k821ffef3: Andorra is a Pyrenean principality landlocked between France and Spain. It has no army; its defense is provided by its two neighbors. Only its police has security assets.
text.ka00f5c95: No armed forces: national police only.
text.kb08dd6b4: A federation of seven emirates on the southern shore of the Persian Gulf, the United Arab Emirates fields one of the most modern and experienced armies in the Arab world. It controls a coastline on the Gulf of Oman that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Its defense industry is growing fast. It was targeted by Iranian strikes during the 2026 war.
text.k8de5d860: Modern Western arsenal (F-16 Block 60, Mirage 2000-9, Leclerc, THAAD, GlobalEye) supplemented by Russian and Chinese equipment. Air defense and regional power projection doctrine.
text.kb5ba1b80: Argentina stretches from the Andes to the South Atlantic and claims the Falkland Islands. Its army, heavily reduced since the 1980s, is gradually re-equipping, notably with F-16s from Denmark. Its navy patrols a vast maritime area reaching the approaches to Antarctica.
text.kc32cc8d8: Ageing arsenal of European and American origin being renewed. Territorial and South Atlantic defense doctrine.
text.kbba4138a: Armenia is a mountainous, landlocked country in the South Caucasus. After losing Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023, it is turning away from Russia and diversifying its suppliers toward India and France. It remains a member of the Collective Security Treaty Organization, though it has frozen its participation, and a Russian base remains at Gyumri.
text.k77031b2c: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin being diversified (CAESAR, Pinaka, Akash). Border defense doctrine.
text.k42ee1e38: Antigua and Barbuda is a small island state in the Lesser Antilles. Its defense force numbers a few hundred personnel. It takes part in the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.kfa49d2f6: A continent-sized country in the southern hemisphere, Australia has vast, sparsely populated lands and a huge maritime zone between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. A close ally of the United States, it is part of the AUKUS partnership, which is to provide it with nuclear attack submarines. Its military is professional, compact and highly modern. Its over-the-horizon radars watch the northern approaches.
text.kbca3959d: Mostly American arsenal (F-35, P-8, E-7, Abrams, HIMARS) plus European equipment (Boxer, frigates). Doctrine of maritime approach defense and long-range strike.
text.k4e3989e3: Austria is a landlocked Alpine country in the heart of Europe. Neutral since 1955, it is not a NATO member but takes part in the European Sky Shield air defense initiative. Its army relies on conscription.
text.k8c2014a1: European arsenal (Typhoon, Leopard 2, Pandur, Ulan). Armed neutrality doctrine.
text.k1e7f955e: Azerbaijan lies on the Caspian Sea and earns substantial revenue from oil and gas. It retook control of Nagorno-Karabakh in 2020 and 2023 thanks to a modernized army. It is closely allied with Turkey.
text.kbdddfde7: Russian arsenal supplemented by Turkish and Israeli drones and missiles (TB2, Harop, Barak 8). Offensive doctrine built on drones and precision strikes.
text.kd2de9f10: Burundi is a small landlocked country in the Great Lakes region. Its armed forces are modest and committed to regional operations. Its troops have served in Somalia and in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
text.k0fe3f8d1: A small, very densely populated country, Belgium hosts the headquarters of NATO and the European Union. Its army, cut back after the Cold War, is being reinvested in. It is renewing its fighter fleet with the F-35 and its land forces with French vehicles. Its North Sea coastline is short but strategic.
text.k3858a700: Light Western arsenal in transition (F-16 to F-35, CaMo program with France). Collective defense and coalition engagement doctrine.
text.k05b087a8: Benin is a coastal country on the Gulf of Guinea facing jihadist incursions in the north. Its armed forces are small. Its army takes part in a regional operation against armed groups from the Sahel.
text.k9bf03018: Burkina Faso is a landlocked Sahel country facing a jihadist insurgency that controls part of its territory. Its army relies on numerous civilian auxiliaries. It has left ECOWAS and formed the Alliance of Sahel States with Mali and Niger.
text.k19c96914: Light forces backed by Turkish drones. Counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.k2582f431: A very densely populated country in the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, Bangladesh is almost entirely surrounded by India and borders the Bay of Bengal. Its armed forces are among the leading contributors to United Nations peacekeeping operations. Its navy protects a large exclusive economic zone in the Bay of Bengal.
text.k75df9961: Mostly Chinese arsenal (tanks, frigates, F-7 fighters) supplemented by Russian equipment. Defensive doctrine for the delta and coastal zone.
text.k49c4a9fd: Bulgaria occupies the eastern Balkans and borders the Black Sea. A NATO member since 2004, it is gradually replacing its Soviet equipment, notably its MiG-29s with F-16 Block 70s. Its industry produces Soviet-caliber ammunition in large quantities.
text.k9d3ec5bc: Mostly Soviet arsenal being replaced (F-16, Stryker). Collective defense and Black Sea security doctrine.
text.k4e2cea3c: An archipelago in the Persian Gulf linked to Saudi Arabia by a causeway, Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet. Its armed forces are small but equipped with modern American materiel. It is a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council and takes part in its joint force.
text.k73c5d989: American arsenal (F-16, Patriot, M60). Coalition defense doctrine with Saudi Arabia and the United States.
text.k8055c4d1: The Bahamas are an Atlantic archipelago off Florida. Their defense force is essentially naval and tasked with maritime surveillance. The archipelago has more than 700 islands scattered over a vast maritime area.
text.kf43d2319: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a mountainous Balkan country with complex institutions born of the Dayton Accords. Its unified armed forces are small and poorly equipped. A European force remains deployed there.
text.kfaf015cf: Light forces with old equipment of Yugoslav and American origin. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k2956789e: Belarus is a land of plains and forests between Poland, the Baltic states, Russia and Ukraine. Closely allied with Russia, it hosts Russian tactical nuclear weapons and served as a staging ground for the 2022 offensive. Its army is mid-sized and equipped with Soviet and Russian materiel.
text.k6ee488b8: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin (T-72B3, BMP-2, S-400, Iskander). Doctrine integrated with Russia's within the Union State.
text.k59701dbc: Belize is a small Central American country on the Caribbean Sea. Its defense force is small and benefits from British cooperation. Guatemala claims part of its territory.
text.kada2929e: Bolivia is a landlocked country spanning the Andes and the Amazon. Its armed forces are modest and equipped with varied materiel, notably Chinese. It maintains a lake and river navy.
text.k1b67bd21: Light arsenal of diverse origins. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k24a995d5: The largest country in Latin America, Brazil covers half of South America and much of the Amazon. It has the region's leading military and a world-class aerospace industry. It assembles its Gripens and submarines locally and is building a nuclear-powered submarine.
text.k3dccf5f9: European and domestic arsenal (Gripen, Leopard 1, Guarani, Scorpène, KC-390, ASTROS). Doctrine of Amazon and South Atlantic defense.
text.k603ea13c: Barbados is the easternmost island of the Lesser Antilles. Its defense force is very small. It takes part in the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.k14180ba5: A small oil sultanate in northern Borneo, Brunei claims part of the South China Sea. Its armed forces are small but well funded and backed by agreements with the United Kingdom and Singapore. Hydrocarbon revenue funds most of its defense budget.
text.k4677b74c: Light European and American arsenal. Doctrine of protecting the territory and oil installations.
text.kdd05b1e1: A Himalayan kingdom landlocked between India and China, Bhutan has a small infantry army. Its defense relies largely on cooperation with India. The Himalayan terrain and border passes form most of its natural defense.
text.k3005d670: Light infantry forces, trained and supported by India.
text.k13a33bb7: Botswana is a landlocked, semi-arid country in southern Africa known for its stability. Its defense force is professional but small. Its army is engaged in anti-poaching efforts and SADC regional operations.
text.kc642da9f: Light forces of Western origin. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.kf3d1223e: The Central African Republic is a landlocked country in central Africa beset by prolonged armed conflicts. Its armed forces are backed by Russian paramilitaries. A United Nations peacekeeping mission has been deployed there since 2014.
text.k0348827d: The world's second-largest country by area, Canada borders three oceans, including the Arctic, where retreating ice is opening new sea routes. It shares the continent's air defense with the United States within NORAD. Its armed forces are professional but small given the size of its territory.
text.k307fb2a1: Mostly American and European arsenal (CF-18s being replaced by the F-35, LAV 6.0, Halifax frigates). Doctrine of continental defense, Arctic sovereignty and coalition engagement.
text.k25166d85: Switzerland is an Alpine country, neutral since 1815. Its militia army can quickly mobilize a large reserve and the terrain lends itself to defense. Its industry produces armored vehicles and air defense systems.
text.ke85bd213: European and American arsenal (F/A-18, F-35 on order, Leopard 2, CV90, Piranha). Doctrine of armed neutrality and defense of the Alpine redoubt.
text.k410a027f: Chile is a long coastal country between the Andes and the Pacific that controls the Strait of Magellan. It has well-equipped, professional armed forces, among the most modern in South America. Its navy exercises sovereignty over Easter Island and a vast area of the South Pacific.
text.k837aa080: Western arsenal (F-16, Leopard 2, British and Dutch frigates, Scorpène). Territorial and maritime defense doctrine.
text.ka0130cc3: The world's second-largest economy, China has the largest army by active personnel and the world's largest navy by number of ships. Its coastline opens onto the East and South China Seas, where its strategic priorities are concentrated, particularly around Taiwan. Its defense industry now produces stealth aircraft, aircraft carriers and hypersonic missiles. Its nuclear arsenal has been growing rapidly since the early 2020s.
text.kfffd51a2: Almost entirely domestic arsenal geared toward area denial: ballistic and anti-ship cruise missiles, integrated air defense, modern combat aviation and a fast-growing blue-water navy.
text.kb9a2799c: Côte d'Ivoire borders the Gulf of Guinea and is one of West Africa's leading economies. Its army, rebuilt after the 2011 crisis, watches the northern border. The French base at Port-Bouët, in Abidjan, was handed back to it in 2025.
text.k45dff9d9: Cameroon stretches from the Gulf of Guinea to Lake Chad. Its armed forces fight Boko Haram in the north and separatists in the English-speaking regions. It takes part in the Lake Chad Basin multinational force.
text.k12d1fce9: Light arsenal of French, Chinese and Israeli origin. Counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.kb03df3bf: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is Africa's second-largest country by area. Its armed forces, numerous but poorly equipped, face multiple armed groups in the east of the country, including the M23. The country shares borders with nine states, several of which are involved in the eastern conflicts.
text.ke4c6fa68: Light arsenal of diverse origins supplemented by Chinese drones. Counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.k87a5c497: The Republic of the Congo borders the Atlantic and the Congo River in central Africa. Its armed forces are modest. Its territory is largely covered by equatorial forest.
text.k191557e4: Light forces with old Soviet equipment.
text.ka245d7db: Colombia borders the Pacific and the Caribbean Sea and controls access to the Isthmus of Panama. Its army, one of the largest in Latin America, has been hardened by decades of fighting guerrillas and drug traffickers. It has ordered Gripens to replace its Kfirs.
text.kdeef067e: American arsenal geared toward counterinsurgency (Black Hawk, Super Tucano). Internal security and territorial control doctrine.
text.k13325caa: The Comoros are an Indian Ocean archipelago between Madagascar and Mozambique. Their armed forces are very small. The archipelago also claims the island of Mayotte, administered by France.
text.kbf22749d: Cape Verde is an Atlantic archipelago off Senegal. Its armed forces are very small. Its Atlantic position makes it a waypoint on the sea routes between Europe, Africa and the Americas.
text.k002729d0: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and devotes its resources to education and health. Its security is provided by the Public Force, a police corps. It is one of the few states in the world with no military force at all.
text.k425b9dc6: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean, 150 km off the coast of Florida. Its armed forces, inherited from Soviet aid, have plentiful but old and poorly maintained equipment. Its doctrine relies on mobilizing the entire population.
text.kd00064d5: Old Soviet arsenal (T-55, MiG-21/23/29, S-75/S-125). Doctrine of the war of all the people.
text.k915549ea: The northern part of Cyprus has been administered since 1974 by an entity recognized only by Turkey. Its own security forces are small, but Turkey stations a large military contingent there. A United Nations buffer zone separates it from the Republic of Cyprus.
text.kb00be8e9: Light security forces, backed by the Turkish contingent stationed on the island.
text.k96fb0f13: The third-largest island in the Mediterranean, Cyprus has been divided since 1974 between the Republic of Cyprus, a member of the European Union, and a northern part administered by a Turkish-backed entity. Its National Guard relies on conscription. It hosts two British sovereign bases.
text.k3a411acc: Arsenal of Russian and Western origin (T-80U, BMP-3, Tor, Barak MX). Doctrine of defending the island until reinforcements arrive.
text.k95dc2eab: A landlocked Central European state, Czechia has a long-established and renowned arms industry, notably for ammunition, vehicles and trainer aircraft. A NATO member since 1999, it is replacing its Soviet equipment with Western materiel. It has played a major role in supplying ammunition to Ukraine.
text.kd159933d: Arsenal in transition (Gripen, L-159, Leopard 2, CV90 on order) and domestic production (Dana, Tatra). Collective defense doctrine within NATO.
text.k52c21501: Europe's largest economy, Germany occupies a central position on the continent, between the North Sea, the Baltic and the Alps. Long restrained in its military ambitions, it has embarked on massive rearmament since 2022 and aims to give Europe its leading conventional army. It has a first-rate defense industry, notably for armored vehicles, submarines and air defense. It stations a permanent brigade in Lithuania.
text.k8d77d199: Mostly domestic and European arsenal (Leopard 2, Puma, PzH 2000, IRIS-T, Typhoon), supplemented by American systems (Patriot, F-35A on order). Collective defense doctrine within NATO.
text.k6a8ac97e: Djibouti controls the African shore of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and hosts French, American, Chinese, Japanese and Italian military bases. Its own armed forces are small. Its position at the entrance to the Red Sea makes it one of the most strategic territories in the region.
text.ke57f4f0e: Light forces; security ensured by the presence of foreign bases.
text.k45b4ccd0: Dominica is a mountainous island in the Lesser Antilles. It has no army; its police provides security. Its defense falls under the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.k57e3142e: Denmark controls the straits linking the Baltic to the North Sea and is responsible for the defense of Greenland and the Faroe Islands. It has sharply increased military spending since 2022 and handed much of its artillery and its F-16s to Ukraine. Its navy operates modern air defense frigates.
text.k37e451db: Compact Western arsenal (F-35, Leopard 2A7, CV90, Iver Huitfeldt frigates). Doctrine of controlling the Baltic straits and supporting allies.
text.k3b88944b: The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola. Its armed forces are relatively large but lightly equipped. Its forces focus on guarding the border with Haiti.
text.ke4417dc3: Light forces of American origin. Internal and border security doctrine.
text.k5fd78954: Africa's largest country, Algeria stretches from the Mediterranean to the heart of the Sahara. It has one of the best-equipped armies on the continent, funded by its hydrocarbon exports. Its air defense is among the densest in Africa. It has received its first Su-57 stealth fighters but lacks the industrial capacity to produce them.
text.k8e3295f9: Mostly Russian arsenal (Su-30MKA, T-90SA, S-300, Pantsir, Kilo submarines). Doctrine of territorial defense and regional deterrence.
text.kdd0ee025: Ecuador borders the Pacific and includes the Galápagos Islands. Its mid-sized armed forces are increasingly engaged against organized crime. Its navy patrols a vast maritime area around the Galápagos.
text.kaa8a765e: Light arsenal of American and European origin. Internal and maritime security doctrine.
text.ke1bebb91: The most populous country in the Arab world, Egypt controls the Suez Canal, linking the Mediterranean to the Red Sea. It has the largest army in Africa and the Middle East by volume of equipment. It diversifies its suppliers among the United States, France, Russia and China. Two Mistral helicopter carriers strengthen its power projection.
text.k5fb65d5e: Very large and diverse arsenal (F-16, Rafale, MiG-29, co-produced Abrams, Mistral, FREMM). Doctrine of Suez Canal defense and regional deterrence.
text.k51c2bfe5: Eritrea lies on the Red Sea opposite Arabia. Open-ended national service lets it field a very large army relative to its population. Its forces fought in the Tigray war alongside Ethiopia.
text.k9f9f3046: Old Soviet arsenal. Mass territorial defense doctrine.
text.k3c4aba1b: Western Sahara is a desert territory of unresolved status, largely administered by Morocco and claimed by the Polisario Front. Polisario forces, based in the east of the territory and in Algeria, are few and lightly equipped. A sand wall more than 2,700 km long separates the areas controlled by Morocco and by the Polisario.
text.k433aec54: Light forces with old Soviet equipment supplied by Algeria. Desert guerrilla doctrine.
text.kcedbe60e: Occupying most of the Iberian Peninsula, Spain controls, together with Morocco, access to the Mediterranean through the Strait of Gibraltar. Its Balearic and Canary archipelagos and its cities of Ceuta and Melilla extend its presence in the Mediterranean and the Atlantic. Its shipbuilding and aerospace industries are substantial and export aircraft carriers and frigates. It is a member of NATO and the European Union.
text.k895506cb: European and American arsenal (Typhoon, Hornet, Leopard 2E, AEGIS frigates). Doctrine centered on defending the maritime approaches and taking part in allied operations.
text.k8d9bdd4c: Estonia is the northernmost Baltic state and shares a border with Russia. Its forces rely on conscription and a large volunteer defense league. It is renowned for its cyber defense expertise and hosts a NATO battlegroup.
text.k7a7863d1: Light, modern arsenal (CV90, K9, HIMARS). Doctrine of total defense, cyber defense and reliance on allies.
text.k1237d44a: Africa's second most populous country, Ethiopia is a landlocked highland nation in the Horn of Africa. Its army, tested by the 2020-2022 Tigray war, remains one of the largest on the continent and makes extensive use of armed drones. It has had no direct access to the sea since Eritrea's independence.
text.k220240c1: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin supplemented by Turkish, Chinese and Iranian drones. Territorial defense and counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.k5f6635aa: Finland shares a border of more than 1,300 km with Russia and joined NATO in 2023. It has kept universal military service and can mobilize a reserve of about 280,000. Its artillery is one of the largest in Europe. Its forested, lake-dotted terrain favors defense in depth.
text.k5f1287ab: Western and domestic arsenal (F/A-18s being replaced by the F-35, Leopard 2, K9, Patria), built on mass territorial defense, plentiful artillery and a large reserve.
text.ked9370b3: Fiji is an archipelago in the South Pacific. Its military forces are small but heavily involved in peacekeeping. Its army also plays an important role in the country's political life.
text.kce6b0cf7: A nuclear power and permanent member of the UN Security Council, France has a full-spectrum military capable of operating alone at long range. Its overseas territories give it the world's second-largest maritime area and a presence in every ocean. It has the only nuclear-powered aircraft carrier outside the United States. Its defense industry designs and produces almost all of its equipment.
text.k9aa0939f: Almost entirely domestic arsenal built for strategic autonomy: sea-based and airborne nuclear deterrence, multirole Rafale aviation, expeditionary forces and a blue-water navy.
text.kb3358769: The Federated States of Micronesia are a Western Pacific archipelago whose defense is provided by the United States. They are linked to the United States by a compact of free association. Their four island states span more than 2,500 km of ocean.
text.keaece2a0: Gabon is a forested, oil-producing country in central Africa. Its armed forces are small. A reduced French military presence is maintained there.
text.k3448bf8c: The Gaza Strip is a 365 km² coastal territory, among the most densely populated in the world. It was devastated by the 2023-2025 war, followed by a ceasefire in October 2025. The armed factions operating there, including the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, have no heavy conventional weapons.
text.kb48abdc3: Light infantry paramilitary forces, without aviation, armor or heavy artillery.
text.k94f236bd: A North Atlantic archipelago, the United Kingdom is a nuclear power and a permanent member of the UN Security Council. Its navy operates two aircraft carriers as well as nuclear attack and ballistic missile submarines. A pillar of NATO, it maintains very close military cooperation with the United States. Its land forces are small but professional and deployable.
text.ke048a5ab: Arsenal mixing domestic and European production (Typhoon, Challenger, Astute) with American equipment (F-35B, Apache, P-8, Trident missiles). Expeditionary and maritime doctrine, integrated into NATO.
text.k0e44b3f6: Georgia lies between the Greater Caucasus and the Black Sea. About 20% of its territory, Abkhazia and South Ossetia, has been beyond its control since the 2008 war with Russia. Its army, trained with Western help, remains modest.
text.k36f22914: Arsenal of Soviet origin supplemented by Western equipment. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k69108c8e: Ghana borders the Gulf of Guinea and is known for its political stability. Its armed forces contribute heavily to peacekeeping. Its navy fights piracy in the Gulf of Guinea.
text.k301adf7b: Light forces of Chinese and Western origin. Maritime security and peacekeeping doctrine.
text.kb23f015c: Guinea lies on the Atlantic in West Africa and has large bauxite reserves. Its armed forces are modest. The country is led by a military government that came to power in the 2021 coup.
text.k849ff27f: The Gambia is a narrow country enclosed by Senegal along the Gambia River. Its armed forces are very small. An ECOWAS mission has been deployed there since 2017.
text.ka1d7c38c: Guinea-Bissau is a small coastal country in West Africa with an unstable political history. Its armed forces are small. Its Bijagós archipelago makes the coastline hard to patrol.
text.k3b018890: Equatorial Guinea is a small oil state in central Africa made up of a mainland region and islands. Its armed forces are small. Its capital, Malabo, lies on the island of Bioko, separated from the mainland.
text.k172ee6d8: Light forces with a few aircraft of Soviet origin.
text.kb56bdec6: An Eastern Mediterranean country with thousands of islands, Greece controls the Aegean Sea and the approaches to the Bosporus. Tense relations with Turkey explain its high defense effort and large combat air force. It is modernizing its forces with Rafales, FDI frigates and F-35s on order.
text.k382f0864: Mostly American and European arsenal (F-16V, Rafale, Leopard, Patriot, Type 214 submarines). Doctrine of Aegean island defense and regional air superiority.
text.k24a07ac6: Grenada is an island state in the Lesser Antilles. It has had no army since 1983; its police provides security. Its defense falls under the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.kdc5681c7: Guatemala is the most populous country in Central America. Its armed forces are mainly engaged in internal security and border surveillance. It claims part of Belize's territory.
text.k7904f4b8: Guyana lies on the Atlantic in northern South America and has large offshore oil reserves. Venezuela claims the Essequibo region, two-thirds of its territory. It is strengthening military cooperation with Brazil and the United States.
text.k89abd7c7: Light forces being reinforced. Territorial defense doctrine with partner support.
text.k3a5dfc0b: Honduras lies at the center of Central America and hosts an American air base. Its armed forces are small and engaged against organized crime. Its Caribbean coast is a transit point for drug trafficking.
text.ka18853f3: Light forces with old equipment. Internal security doctrine.
text.k732c654b: Croatia stretches along the Adriatic coast and into the Pannonian Plain. A NATO member since 2009, it has acquired second-hand Rafales and Bradleys. Its army is professional and small.
text.k9dbb92b7: Arsenal being modernized (Rafale, Bradley, Patria, PzH 2000). Collective defense doctrine.
text.k1721bd04: Haiti occupies the western third of the island of Hispaniola. Its armed forces, disbanded in 1995 and re-formed since 2017, remain embryonic in the face of armed gangs. A multinational security support mission backs the national police.
text.k83dae714: A land of plains at the center of the Carpathian Basin, Hungary is a member of NATO and the European Union. It is modernizing its army with German equipment and hosts a Lynx armored vehicle plant. It pursues a foreign policy distinct from its allies' on several issues.
text.kdd6d3d93: Recent European arsenal (Gripen, Leopard 2A7, Lynx, PzH 2000, NASAMS). Territorial defense doctrine.
text.kf416f035: The world's largest archipelago with more than 17,000 islands, Indonesia controls straits vital to world trade, including Malacca and Sunda. The fourth most populous country, it has a large army spread across its territory. It is modernizing its navy and air force with Rafales and submarines. It pursues a non-aligned foreign policy.
text.kfb4be953: Highly diverse arsenal (American, Russian, European, South Korean) being modernized. Archipelagic defense and strait security doctrine.
text.k74ed0f1f: The world's most populous country, India occupies the Indian subcontinent between the Himalayas and the Indian Ocean. Long-standing border disputes with Pakistan and China shape its military posture. A nuclear power, it fields one of the world's largest armies and two aircraft carriers. Its defense industry is advancing, often through foreign licenses and joint ventures.
text.ka5b2b98f: Heterogeneous, mainly Russian arsenal (Su-30MKI, T-90, T-72) supplemented by French, Israeli and American equipment and growing domestic production. Priority on the two northern land fronts and control of the Indian Ocean.
text.k70d50dfd: Ireland occupies most of the island of Ireland, west of Great Britain. Neutral, it has small defense forces and no combat aviation. Its navy patrols a vast area of the North Atlantic.
text.k6ee43606: Light forces with European equipment. Neutrality and peacekeeping doctrine.
text.k1739cc2c: A vast plateau between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf, Iran controls the northern shore of the Strait of Hormuz, through which much of the world's oil passes. Since February 2026 it has been at war with the United States and Israel, whose strikes destroyed much of its air force, navy and air defenses. It retains a large arsenal of ballistic missiles and drones and relies on a network of allied armed groups in the region. Its population exceeds 90 million.
text.k1a143ffc: Old arsenal of American and Soviet origin, largely replaced by domestic production of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and attack drones. Asymmetric doctrine of deterrence through saturation and control of the Strait of Hormuz.
text.k41da3a7a: Iraq stretches between the Tigris and Euphrates, from the Turkish border to the Persian Gulf. Its army, rebuilt after 2003 and again after the war against the Islamic State, combines American and Russian equipment. Iran-aligned militias of the Popular Mobilization Forces coexist with the regular forces.
text.k04a13198: Mixed American and Russian arsenal (F-16IQ, Abrams, T-90, Mi-28). Counterinsurgency and border defense doctrine.
text.kbbcd26c1: Iceland is a volcanic North Atlantic island with no army and a founding member of NATO. Its position between Greenland and Europe makes it key to monitoring the GIUK gap. Its coast guard carries out sovereignty missions.
text.k2e5882c5: No armed forces: coast guard and a response unit; defense provided by allies.
text.k5fcbd299: A small territory between the Mediterranean and the Jordan Valley, Israel has one of the most powerful militaries in the Middle East, based on conscription and a large mobilizable reserve. At war on several fronts since 2023, in Gaza, Lebanon and against Iran, it has demonstrated its long-range strike capability. It has a layered missile defense unique in the world. It neither confirms nor denies having nuclear weapons.
text.kf7c8b2ef: American air arsenal (F-35I, F-15, F-16) and cutting-edge domestic production (Merkava, drones, Iron Dome, Arrow, missiles). Doctrine of technological superiority, preemptive strike and missile defense.
text.k27a489fc: A peninsula at the center of the Mediterranean, Italy commands the passages between the eastern and western basins. It has a sizable navy with two aircraft carriers able to operate the F-35B. Its defense industry is a leader in helicopters, ships and electronics. It hosts major NATO and US bases.
text.k139b58b9: Mostly domestic and European arsenal (Typhoon, FREMM, Ariete, Leonardo helicopters) supplemented by the F-35. Priority on the Mediterranean and NATO collective defense.
text.k28483acf: Jamaica is an island in the Greater Antilles. Its small defense force supports the police in fighting crime. It takes part in the Caribbean regional security system.
text.kd0d94fff: Light forces. Internal and maritime security doctrine.
text.k174fedb3: Jordan holds a pivotal position between Israel, Syria, Iraq and Saudi Arabia. Its professional army is known for its discipline and special forces. It hosts allied forces and was targeted by strikes in 2026.
text.k604e2347: American and British arsenal (F-16, Challenger 1, M60, Patriot). Border defense and regional security doctrine.
text.kafccf203: An archipelago of nearly 7,000 islands off the Asian mainland, Japan is the world's fourth-largest economy. Its pacifist constitution constrains its Self-Defense Forces, which are nonetheless among the best equipped in Asia. It has committed to doubling its defense budget and is acquiring long-range strike capabilities. Its territory extends to islands close to Taiwan, at the heart of regional tensions.
text.ka30eb124: American arsenal largely built under license (F-15J, F-35, Patriot, SM-3) and high-tech domestic equipment (F-2, Type 10, Taigei submarines). Defensive doctrine focused on missile and maritime defense.
text.kaf22eef0: The world's ninth-largest country by area, Kazakhstan stretches from the Caspian Sea to the Altai Mountains, between Russia and China. It hosts the Baikonur Cosmodrome. Its armed forces are the largest in Central Asia.
text.k4f73c57e: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin (Su-30SM, MiG-31, T-72) with local production of radars and vehicles. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k20f8d9b9: Kenya borders the Indian Ocean and Somalia, where its troops are engaged against al-Shabaab. Its armed forces are professional and benefit from American and British cooperation. Its navy watches the maritime approaches to Mombasa, East Africa's leading port.
text.kcff7f144: Light arsenal of Western and Chinese origin. Counterinsurgency and regional security doctrine.
text.kbac67e2f: Kyrgyzstan is a mountainous Central Asian country that hosts a Russian air base. Its armed forces are small. It has border tensions with Tajikistan.
text.k36e4548e: Soviet arsenal supplemented by Turkish drones. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k42135941: Cambodia occupies the south of the Indochinese Peninsula and opens onto the Gulf of Thailand. Ream Naval Base, modernized with Chinese help, now hosts Chinese corvettes. Its army is large but poorly equipped.
text.kb4fb6a73: Old arsenal of Soviet origin supplemented by recent Chinese equipment. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k00b6f992: Kiribati is a state of atolls scattered across the central Pacific. It has no army. Its exclusive economic zone is one of the largest in the Pacific.
text.kaa5e6c9c: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign state in the Americas. Its defense force numbers a few hundred personnel. It takes part in the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.k8add0b5f: South Korea occupies the southern half of the Korean Peninsula, separated from the North by the Demilitarized Zone since the 1953 armistice. It maintains a large army, backed by the presence of American forces. Its defense industry has become one of the world's leading exporters, notably of tanks, artillery and trainer aircraft. Its capital lies within range of North Korean artillery.
text.kfc51209f: Modern domestic arsenal (K2, K9, KF-21, KDX-III destroyers) and American equipment (F-35, F-15K, Patriot). Doctrine of deterrence and preemptive strike against North Korea.
text.k843ac691: A small oil emirate at the head of the Persian Gulf, Kuwait borders Iraq and Saudi Arabia. Invaded by Iraq in 1990, it has rebuilt a well-equipped army and hosts large American forces. Its flat desert territory offers few natural obstacles.
text.k1a842884: American and European arsenal (Super Hornet, Typhoon, Abrams, Patriot). Doctrine of territorial defense in coalition.
text.k39f00523: The only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, Laos is crossed by the Mekong and surrounded by more powerful neighbors. Its army is modest and relies heavily on Russian, Chinese and Vietnamese aid. Its mountainous, forested terrain favors territorial defense.
text.ke8b40026: Light arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin (T-72B1, Yak-130). Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k3f76e22b: A small mountainous country on the Levantine coast, Lebanon is marked by the presence of Hezbollah, whose armed wing has an arsenal independent of the national army. The south of the country was the scene of wars with Israel in 2024 and 2026. The Lebanese army, supported by the United States and France, remains poorly equipped.
text.k64ae4981: Light arsenal of American and European origin. Doctrine of internal security and preserving national cohesion.
text.k3bf0172d: Liberia lies on the Atlantic in West Africa. Its armed forces were entirely rebuilt after the civil war and remain very small. Its army takes part in United Nations peacekeeping operations.
text.k1cdc8ea4: Libya has Africa's largest oil reserves and a long Mediterranean coastline. The country remains divided between a government in the west and the Libyan National Army in the east, each backed by foreign powers. Its forces are fragmented into regular units and militias.
text.kb8beed51: Remnants of Soviet equipment supplemented by foreign deliveries (Turkish drones, Pantsir). Forces split between two rival authorities.
text.kb3ed12fa: Saint Lucia is an island in the Lesser Antilles. It has no army; its police has a special unit. Its defense falls under the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.k0b6366f9: Liechtenstein is an Alpine principality landlocked between Switzerland and Austria. It abolished its army in 1868. Only its national police ensures the territory's security.
text.k8eae05f1: An Indian Ocean island off the southern tip of India, Sri Lanka holds a central position on the sea routes between Asia and the Middle East. Its army, greatly expanded during the civil war that ended in 2009, is being reduced. The port of Hambantota, developed with Chinese capital, occupies a strategic position on these routes.
text.kaeabca3f: Old, heterogeneous arsenal of Chinese, Russian and Israeli origin. Internal security and maritime surveillance doctrine.
text.k04db9e87: Lesotho is a mountainous kingdom entirely enclosed by South Africa. Its armed forces are very small. Its highland terrain makes it hard to access.
text.k5432cf11: Lithuania is the largest Baltic state and controls the Suwałki corridor, between Belarus and the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad. It hosts a permanent German brigade. It devotes more than 3% of its GDP to defense.
text.kb6963f88: Light, modern arsenal (Boxer, PzH 2000, CAESAR, NASAMS, HIMARS). Doctrine of forward defense and defense of the Suwałki corridor.
text.kb46430da: Luxembourg is a small country landlocked between Belgium, France and Germany. Its army is the smallest in NATO. It contributes mainly through airlift and satellite communications capabilities.
text.ke82846c2: Light forces, support capabilities pooled with Belgium. Collective defense doctrine.
text.kbe182a95: Latvia lies at the center of the Baltic states and borders Russia and Belarus. It reinstated conscription in 2023 and hosts a NATO multinational brigade led by Canada. Its eastern border with Russia and Belarus is being fortified.
text.kad33c756: Light arsenal being modernized (M109, HIMARS, Patria vehicles). Forward defense doctrine alongside allies.
text.kab6715cd: Morocco borders both the Mediterranean and the Atlantic and faces Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar. It claims Western Sahara, most of which it administers. It is modernizing its army with American and Israeli equipment.
text.k6c0a6bf0: Mostly American (F-16, Abrams, Apache) and European arsenal, supplemented by Turkish and Israeli drones. Doctrine of Saharan defense and regional deterrence.
text.k7866b8de: Monaco is a city-state on the Mediterranean coast enclosed by French territory. Its defense is provided by France. The Prince's Company of Carabiniers guards the sovereign.
text.ke6a6a56d: No armed forces: princely guard and police.
text.kf23c25e1: Moldova is a small country landlocked between Romania and Ukraine. The separatist region of Transnistria, where Russian troops are stationed, is beyond its control. Its army is very small and being modernized.
text.k13dbc2ad: Light forces with old equipment, reinforced by European donations. Neutrality doctrine.
text.k7c07ac94: Madagascar is the world's fourth-largest island, in the Indian Ocean. Its armed forces are small. Its position on the Mozambique Channel gives it strategic importance for sea routes.
text.k3ca65c1a: The Maldives are an Indian Ocean archipelago on major sea routes. Their national defense force is small and has a few armed drones. The archipelago has nearly 1,200 low-lying islands spread over more than 800 km.
text.kbc7b1fbd: Light forces, coast guard and Turkish drones.
text.kdc20cee3: Mexico stretches between the United States and Central America and borders the Pacific and the Gulf of Mexico. Its armed forces are mainly engaged in internal security and the fight against cartels. It has neither tanks nor modern combat aviation.
text.keac9b429: Light arsenal geared toward internal security (helicopters, patrol boats, light vehicles). Internal security and maritime surveillance doctrine.
text.kf13625be: The Marshall Islands are a Pacific atoll state whose defense is provided by the United States. They host an American missile test site. Their atolls cover a vast area of the central Pacific.
text.k3a766e33: North Macedonia is a landlocked Balkan country, a NATO member since 2020. Its army is small and has given part of its Soviet equipment to Ukraine. It is re-equipping with Western materiel.
text.k13a2ef92: Light forces transitioning to Western equipment. Collective defense doctrine.
text.k29829adb: Mali is a vast landlocked Sahel country. Since the departure of French and UN forces, its army has been fighting jihadist groups with the support of Russian paramilitaries. It has left ECOWAS and formed the Alliance of Sahel States with Burkina Faso and Niger.
text.ka114f730: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin supplemented by Turkish drones. Counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.k33190817: Malta is an archipelago in the middle of the Mediterranean, between Sicily and North Africa. Neutral, it has small armed forces focused mainly on maritime surveillance. Its port of Valletta holds a key position on Mediterranean sea routes.
text.k8d401fee: Light forces and patrol boats. Neutrality and maritime surveillance doctrine.
text.k5923775b: Myanmar stretches from the Bay of Bengal to the Himalayan foothills and shares long borders with China and India. Since the 2021 coup, the army has faced a nationwide insurgency that has cost it control of vast regions. Its actual strength has fallen sharply.
text.k800dab59: Chinese and Russian arsenal (MiG-29, Su-30, Yak-130, Chinese tanks). Counterinsurgency doctrine relying on air power and artillery.
text.kfacd9c82: Montenegro is a small Balkan country with a rugged Adriatic coastline. A NATO member since 2017, it has very small armed forces. Its navy consists of a few patrol boats.
text.k751afd2a: Light forces without heavy equipment. Collective defense doctrine.
text.ke0512126: Landlocked between Russia and China, Mongolia is one of the most sparsely populated states in the world. Its armed forces are modest and equipped with old Soviet materiel. It is an active contributor to peacekeeping operations.
text.kced7d6e1: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin. Defensive doctrine of neutrality between its two large neighbors.
text.k3d3e9c96: Mozambique borders the Indian Ocean in southern Africa. Its small armed forces are fighting a jihadist insurgency in the north of the country with Rwandan support. Its long coastline runs along the Mozambique Channel, rich in natural gas.
text.k1bb1f3d6: Light forces with old Soviet equipment. Counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.k28675f38: Mauritania stretches from the Atlantic to the Sahara, between the Maghreb and sub-Saharan Africa. Its army has implemented an effective desert control strategy. It remains an important security partner of European countries in the Sahel.
text.k453f69af: Mobile light forces and light support aviation. Desert control doctrine.
text.k77cf1f4f: Mauritius is an Indian Ocean island state without an army. Its security relies on the Special Mobile Force, a paramilitary police unit. Its coast guard patrols a vast exclusive economic zone.
text.k0a6599c5: Malawi is a landlocked country in southern Africa bordering Lake Malawi. Its armed forces are small. Its troops take part in SADC regional operations.
text.kb523cca0: Malaysia is split between the Malay Peninsula and northern Borneo, separated by the South China Sea. It borders the Strait of Malacca and claims part of the Spratlys. Its armed forces are mid-sized and of very diverse origins.
text.kbc5c90c2: Heterogeneous arsenal (Su-30MKM, F/A-18, Hawk, PT-91, Scorpène). Maritime defense and strait security doctrine.
text.k028c7fc5: Namibia lies on the Atlantic in southern Africa and includes the Namib Desert. Its armed forces are small and equipped with Chinese materiel. Its Atlantic coast is home to the deep-water port of Walvis Bay.
text.kf7f56c12: Light forces of Chinese origin. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.kf0b837e2: Niger is a vast landlocked Sahel country. Since the 2023 coup, it has moved closer to Mali and Burkina Faso and is fighting jihadist groups on several fronts. It has left ECOWAS and demanded the departure of French and American forces.
text.k76ba57ce: Africa's most populous country, Nigeria borders the Gulf of Guinea and has substantial oil resources. Its armed forces are engaged against jihadist groups in the northeast, banditry and maritime piracy. Its navy is the largest in West Africa.
text.ka702a17b: Diverse arsenal (JF-17, Super Tucano, Chinese tanks, Russian helicopters). Counterinsurgency and maritime security doctrine.
text.k9a9dfc51: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America and borders both oceans. Its modest army retains equipment of Soviet and Russian origin. It maintains military cooperation with Russia.
text.k46d56bb0: Light arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.kbf17c6f4: A low-lying country at the mouth of the Rhine, the Netherlands is home to Europe's largest port. It has a compact professional army whose land forces are closely integrated with Germany's. Its navy is renowned for its radars and air defense frigates. It was among the first European countries to replace all its F-16s with F-35s.
text.k978ecf03: High-tech Western arsenal (F-35, CV90, Boxer, Patriot, De Zeven Provinciën frigates). Collective defense doctrine integrated into NATO and German-Dutch cooperation.
text.k932cd796: A mountainous country with a deeply indented coastline, Norway controls access to the Barents Sea and shares an Arctic border with Russia. Thanks to its oil revenue, it maintains modern forces despite a small population. Its defense industry is renowned for its anti-ship missiles and air defense. It plays a key role in monitoring the High North for NATO.
text.k8361606a: Modern Western arsenal (F-35, P-8, CV90, K9, NASAMS, NSM missiles). Doctrine of High North defense and maritime surveillance.
text.k076e5063: A Himalayan country landlocked between India and China, Nepal has a large but light army, heir to the Gurkha military tradition. It is a major contributor to peacekeeping operations. Its soldiers also serve in the Gurkha regiments of the British and Indian armies.
text.k04cf9d93: Mainly infantry forces with Indian and Chinese equipment. Territorial defense and internal security doctrine.
text.kfe669e34: Nauru is a small island in the central Pacific. It has no army; its defense is provided by Australia. It is one of the smallest states in the world.
text.k9c3b5aa8: A South Pacific archipelago far from the main zones of tension, New Zealand has a small, professional defense force. It patrols a vast maritime area and Pacific territories. It gave up its combat aviation in 2001.
text.k7baabf72: Light Western arsenal (P-8, C-130J, Anzac frigates). Maritime surveillance and coalition participation doctrine.
text.k1ddd8ed6: The Sultanate of Oman occupies the southeastern corner of the Arabian Peninsula and controls the southern shore of the Strait of Hormuz through the Musandam Peninsula. It pursues a neutral foreign policy and often serves as a regional mediator. Its armed forces are mid-sized and British-equipped.
text.kf8b39dec: British and American arsenal (Typhoon, F-16, Challenger 2). Coastal defense and strait security doctrine.
text.k46a3015c: Pakistan stretches from the Arabian Sea to the Himalayas, between India, Afghanistan, Iran and China. A nuclear power, it maintains a large army shaped by its rivalry with India, with which it clashed in May 2025. Its Afghan border is the scene of fighting against armed groups and clashes with the Taliban. China is its main arms supplier.
text.ka9820ecd: Mostly Chinese (co-produced JF-17, J-10C, tanks, Type 054A frigates) and American (F-16) arsenal. Doctrine of nuclear deterrence and defense against India.
text.k311d76b9: Panama controls the canal linking the Atlantic to the Pacific. It has had no army since 1990; its security is provided by public police, border and coast guard forces. The canal is a strategic artery for world navies and trade.
text.k81e577b7: No armed forces: public security forces.
text.kb5ef923c: Peru stretches from the Pacific coast across the Andes to the Amazon. Its armed forces are mid-sized and equipped with Russian and European materiel. Its navy has a large submarine fleet.
text.k5190b361: Mixed Russian and European arsenal (MiG-29, Mirage 2000, Type 209). Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k65fcf8dc: An archipelago of more than 7,000 islands between the South China Sea and the Pacific, the Philippines is bound to the United States by a mutual defense treaty. It faces growing tensions with China over the Spratly reefs. Its army, long focused on internal security, is reorienting toward external defense.
text.kaf9d2da5: Light arsenal, mainly American and South Korean (FA-50, Jose Rizal frigates), supplemented by BrahMos missiles. Archipelagic defense doctrine under construction.
text.ka0c85b13: Palau is a Western Pacific archipelago whose defense is provided by the United States. It is linked to the United States by a compact of free association. The archipelago holds a forward position facing the Philippines.
text.k903bb17b: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of New Guinea and many islands. Its defense force is small and supported by Australia. Its mountainous, forested terrain makes internal communications very difficult.
text.k92a1fa91: At the heart of the great European plain, Poland borders the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad, Belarus and Ukraine. It now devotes one of NATO's highest shares of GDP to defense and is building one of Europe's largest land armies. It is buying American and South Korean equipment on a massive scale, partly produced under license. It serves as a hub for military aid to Ukraine.
text.kcf2ea8fd: Arsenal rapidly transitioning from its Soviet legacy to American and Korean equipment (Abrams, K2, K9, HIMARS, Patriot, F-35). Doctrine of forward defense and massive conventional deterrence.
text.keedd3222: North Korea occupies the northern half of the Korean Peninsula under a closed regime that devotes a considerable share of its resources to the military. It fields more than a million active soldiers and massive artillery deployed near the Demilitarized Zone. It has developed nuclear weapons and intercontinental missiles. It has supplied ammunition, missiles and troops to Russia since 2023.
text.k5cce83c0: Old arsenal of Soviet and Chinese origin, offset by sheer mass, long-range artillery, very numerous special forces and an expanding ballistic and nuclear arsenal.
text.k7b94c009: Located at the southwestern tip of Europe, Portugal has a vast maritime area thanks to the Azores and Madeira archipelagos. A founding member of NATO, it controls strategic Atlantic positions, including Lajes Air Base. Its armed forces are modest and geared toward maritime surveillance.
text.kb6fd5cb4: Modest Western arsenal (F-16, MEKO frigates, Type 214 submarines). Priority on Atlantic surveillance and allied operations.
text.k64508edf: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the heart of South America, between Brazil, Argentina and Bolivia. Its armed forces are small and poorly equipped. It shares the Itaipú Dam, one of the largest in the world, with Brazil.
text.kd6da6f1f: Light forces with old equipment. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.kebac25c6: The Palestinian Authority administers part of the West Bank. It has no army but security services and police forces trained with international help. Its territory is fragmented and surrounded by Israel and Jordan.
text.kcea64f93: Paramilitary security forces with small arms and no heavy equipment.
text.kce998095: A gas-rich peninsula in the Persian Gulf, Qatar hosts the region's main American air base at Al Udeid. It has invested heavily in its combat air force, equipped with three types of Western aircraft. Its fighters shot down two Iranian bombers in March 2026. It acts as a mediator in several regional conflicts.
text.k769f9be8: Recent Western arsenal (Rafale, F-15QA, Typhoon, Leopard 2A7, Patriot). Doctrine of air defense and security of gas installations.
text.k71617f15: Romania borders the Black Sea and Ukraine and forms NATO's southeastern flank. It hosts an American missile defense site and a reinforced allied presence. It is buying American equipment on a massive scale and producing Piranha vehicles locally.
text.kdc388b09: Arsenal transitioning from its Soviet legacy to Western equipment (F-16, Patriot, HIMARS, Abrams on order). Doctrine of Black Sea and eastern flank defense.
text.kd9c14681: The largest country in the world, Russia stretches from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific and has long Arctic and maritime coastlines. It has the largest nuclear arsenal on the planet and a defense industry able to produce the full range of modern weapons. Engaged since 2022 in a high-intensity war in Ukraine, it has suffered heavy equipment losses while sharply increasing its manpower and production. Its Northern and Pacific Fleets hold most of its strategic submarines.
text.k1cf132b0: Domestic arsenal marked by massed artillery and armor, dense layered air defense and intensive use of cruise missiles, glide bombs and attack drones. Nuclear deterrence remains at the core of its doctrine.
text.k7fd07037: Rwanda is a small, landlocked, densely populated country in the Great Lakes region. Its highly disciplined army is engaged in several African countries. Its troops are deployed in Mozambique and the Central African Republic.
text.k76e729dc: Battle-hardened light forces. Regional intervention doctrine.
text.k09c59fc3: Occupying most of the Arabian Peninsula, Saudi Arabia borders the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf and holds some of the world's largest oil reserves. It has one of the largest defense budgets on the planet and is the Middle East's leading arms importer. Its oil infrastructure and cities have repeatedly been targeted by missiles and drones from Yemen and Iran.
text.ke68bf325: Very modern American and British arsenal (F-15SA, Typhoon, Abrams, Patriot, THAAD). Doctrine of territorial air defense and regional intervention.
text.k5f984c56: Sudan is a vast Sahel country bordering the Red Sea. Since April 2023, the regular army has been fighting the Rapid Support Forces in a devastating civil war. The country is effectively divided between the two sides.
text.ka15bd753: Arsenal of Soviet, Russian and Chinese origin, supplemented by Iranian and Turkish drones. Civil war doctrine relying on air power and artillery.
text.k77a83206: Senegal occupies the westernmost tip of Africa and controls rich fishing waters. Its army is professional and known for its stability. French forces left the country in 2025.
text.kba4181c0: Light forces and a surveillance navy. Maritime and regional security doctrine.
text.k417cef82: A city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula, Singapore commands the Strait of Malacca, one of the busiest sea lanes in the world. Despite its small size, it devotes a major effort to defense and has some of the most modern forces in Southeast Asia. National service lets it mobilize a large reserve.
text.k3f1723bd: Modern arsenal of American, European and domestic origin (F-15SG, F-16, Leopard 2, Hunter). Doctrine of deterrence through technological superiority and rapid mobilization.
text.kab3872b1: The Solomon Islands are a Melanesian archipelago in the South Pacific. They have no army; their police provides security. A security agreement links them to Australia and another to China.
text.kd40e7287: Sierra Leone lies on the Atlantic in West Africa. Its armed forces were rebuilt with British help after the civil war. Its troops take part in peacekeeping operations.
text.k6f5c26e0: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America and the only one without a Caribbean coast. Its army works alongside the police against gangs. It is one of the most densely populated countries in the Americas.
text.k9069916f: San Marino is a small republic enclosed by Italy and one of the oldest states in the world. It has no operational army. Its military corps are essentially ceremonial.
text.k39fa400f: No operational armed forces: ceremonial corps and gendarmerie.
text.k5d604a44: Somaliland is a territory in northwestern Somalia that declared independence in 1991 without international recognition. It borders the Gulf of Aden and has the port of Berbera. It has its own army and its own currency.
text.kd55e4969: Somalia borders the Indian Ocean and the Gulf of Aden. Its national army, supported by the African Union and Turkey, fights al-Shabaab. Its long coastline runs along sea routes exposed to piracy.
text.k03d59db8: A landlocked country in the heart of the Balkans, Serbia practices military neutrality between NATO and Russia. It buys Russian and Chinese equipment while ordering French Rafales. Its arms industry produces artillery and ammunition.
text.k1e019036: Arsenal of Soviet and Yugoslav origin supplemented by Russian, Chinese and soon French purchases. Armed neutrality doctrine.
text.kbf4d60f9: South Sudan, independent since 2011, is a landlocked country in East Africa. Its army is large but poorly equipped and scarred by the divisions of the civil war. The country is rich in oil but depends on Sudan to export it.
text.k0ec4be71: Light forces with old Soviet equipment. Internal security doctrine.
text.kb365fb31: São Tomé and Príncipe is a small archipelago in the Gulf of Guinea. Its armed forces are very small. It lies at the heart of an oil-producing area of the Gulf of Guinea.
text.k10bffede: Suriname is a small forested country in northern South America. Its army is very small. It shares borders with French Guiana and Guyana.
text.kc4ce3377: Slovakia is a mountainous, landlocked Central European country bordering Ukraine. It has replaced its MiG-29s, given to Ukraine, with F-16 Block 70s. Its industry produces self-propelled artillery and ammunition.
text.kbc3c4591: Arsenal transitioning to Western equipment (F-16, CV90, Patria) with domestic artillery (Zuzana 2). Collective defense doctrine.
text.k674dc204: Slovenia is a small Alpine country with a short Adriatic coastline. Its small professional army takes part in NATO collective defense. It has no combat aviation; its air policing is provided by allies.
text.k33ed47d3: Light forces with Western equipment (Patria, IRIS-T SLM). Collective defense doctrine.
text.k7eb78358: A long Scandinavian peninsula on the Baltic, Sweden joined NATO in 2024 after two centuries of non-alignment. It has a complete defense industry able to design its own combat aircraft, submarines and armored vehicles. The island of Gotland holds a key position in the middle of the Baltic. It has reinstated military service and total defense.
text.k2d949459: Almost entirely domestic arsenal (Gripen, CV90, Archer, AIP submarines, GlobalEye). Doctrine of Baltic defense and whole-of-society resilience.
text.k2eb25099: Eswatini is a small kingdom landlocked between South Africa and Mozambique. Its armed forces are small. It is one of the last absolute monarchies in the world.
text.kec82b4b1: The Seychelles are an Indian Ocean archipelago. Their defense force is very small and focused on maritime surveillance. The archipelago has 115 islands scattered over a vast area of the Indian Ocean.
text.keb04c3c4: Syria occupies the heart of the Levant, between the Mediterranean, Turkey, Iraq and Israel. After the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime in December 2024, a new army is being formed from former rebel factions and the Syrian Democratic Forces. Israeli strikes destroyed most of the former army's aircraft, navy and stockpiles.
text.kb244049b: Remnants of Soviet and Russian equipment, being reorganized with Turkish help. Internal security and reconstruction doctrine.
text.kfd3dce89: Chad is a vast landlocked Sahel country. Its army, known for its fighting spirit, is engaged against jihadist groups around Lake Chad. French forces left the country in early 2025.
text.k26678522: Light arsenal of Soviet origin supplemented by Turkish drones. Mobile counterinsurgency doctrine.
text.kec19e7cb: Togo is a narrow coastal country on the Gulf of Guinea. Its army faces jihadist incursions in the north. Its port of Lomé is an important sea outlet for the Sahel.
text.k563e732e: Light forces backed by Turkish drones.
text.k81df45b9: Thailand occupies the heart of the Indochinese Peninsula and borders both the Andaman Sea and the Gulf of Thailand. A historic ally of the United States, it also buys Chinese and Swedish equipment. The army plays an important political role. Its light aircraft carrier is the only one in Southeast Asia.
text.k86bd2e32: Diverse arsenal (F-16, Gripen, Stryker, VT-4, Chinese and Korean frigates). Territorial defense and regional maritime security doctrine.
text.k56bb9512: Tajikistan is a very mountainous Central Asian country bordering Afghanistan and China. Russia maintains its largest foreign military base there. Its armed forces are few in number.
text.k0c552b89: Limited Soviet arsenal. Border security doctrine with Russian support.
text.k696a9fcb: Turkmenistan borders the Caspian Sea and has large gas reserves. It officially declares itself neutral. Its army is mid-sized and mixes Soviet, Turkish and Chinese equipment.
text.k074077f2: Soviet arsenal supplemented by Turkish, Chinese and Italian purchases. Defensive neutrality doctrine.
text.k8156a7f4: East Timor, independent since 2002, occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor. Its defense forces are very small and consist mainly of light infantry. Its position separates Indonesia from Australia.
text.k55aa3062: Light forces without heavy equipment, backed by partnerships with Australia and Portugal.
text.k2fe8e262: Tonga is an island kingdom in the South Pacific. Its armed forces are very small. Its soldiers have taken part in international operations.
text.kecbf2040: Trinidad and Tobago is a hydrocarbon-rich Lesser Antilles archipelago close to Venezuela. Its defense force is small. It lies about ten kilometers off the Venezuelan coast.
text.k0a06124e: Light forces and coast guard. Maritime security doctrine.
text.k1de181db: The smallest country in the Maghreb, Tunisia holds a central position in the Mediterranean opposite Sicily. Its modest, professional army focuses mainly on securing the borders with Libya and Algeria. Its army is known for its political neutrality.
text.kba23c404: Light arsenal of American origin. Border security and counterterrorism doctrine.
text.kfcb4a3a5: Straddling Europe and Asia, Turkey controls the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits, the Black Sea's only access to the Mediterranean. It has NATO's second-largest army by personnel. Its defense industry has grown spectacularly, notably in armed drones, ships and armored vehicles. It pursues an active regional policy from the Caucasus to Libya.
text.k4ad1bb9d: Arsenal of American and German origin increasingly replaced by domestic production (Bayraktar drones, T129, Altay, MILGEM frigates, missiles). Doctrine of strategic autonomy and regional power projection.
text.keb01a9dc: Tuvalu is a small Pacific atoll state. It has no army. Its low-lying islands are particularly threatened by rising seas.
text.k10f3c6c0: Taiwan is a 36,000 km² island separated from mainland China by a strait 130 to 180 km wide. Its political status is disputed and its defense is built around the scenario of an invasion from the mainland. Its mountainous terrain and limited landing beaches favor the defender. It produces a large share of the world's advanced semiconductors.
text.k0f62bb48: American (F-16V, Abrams, HIMARS, Patriot) and domestic (Tien Kung, Hsiung Feng) arsenal. "Porcupine" defense doctrine based on anti-ship missiles, air defense and dispersal.
text.k3e68ad5f: Tanzania borders the Indian Ocean and the great lakes of East Africa. Its armed forces are mainly equipped with Chinese materiel. It takes part in peacekeeping operations, notably in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
text.kcdab5fdb: Light arsenal of Chinese origin. Territorial defense doctrine.
text.k1d5d8050: Uganda is a landlocked country in the Great Lakes region. Its army is battle-hardened by deployments in Somalia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It hosts one of the largest refugee populations in Africa.
text.k649c1545: Arsenal of Soviet and Russian origin (T-90S, Su-30MK2). Regional security doctrine.
text.k4ce92a51: Europe's second-largest country by area, Ukraine stretches from the Carpathians to the Sea of Azov and borders the Black Sea. Since February 2022 it has resisted a full-scale Russian invasion that occupies part of its territory. Its army, now one of the most experienced in Europe, combines Soviet and Western equipment. It has built a massive drone and cruise missile industry.
text.ka69339a5: Mixed arsenal in full transformation: Soviet legacy (T-64, BMP, S-300) and Western equipment (F-16, Leopard, Bradley, HIMARS, Patriot). High-intensity warfare doctrine built on drones, deep strikes and air defense.
text.kfe9262d0: Uruguay is a small Atlantic country between Argentina and Brazil. Its armed forces are modest and heavily involved in peacekeeping operations. Its navy patrols the Río de la Plata estuary.
text.k75d94c0a: The world's third-largest country by area and population, the United States borders both the Atlantic and the Pacific and has the world's largest economy. It accounts for more than a third of global military spending and maintains a network of bases and alliances on every continent, including NATO. Its carrier-based naval air power, built around eleven aircraft carriers, lets it project considerable force over long distances. Its nuclear triad comprises intercontinental missiles, ballistic missile submarines and strategic bombers.
text.k84974f94: Almost entirely domestic, latest-generation arsenal built on air superiority, power projection and long-range precision strikes. Munitions stockpiles were heavily depleted by the 2026 Iran war.
text.k46f64887: The most populous country in Central Asia, Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked and borders Afghanistan. Its army is the largest in the region after Kazakhstan's. It does not belong to any military alliance.
text.kef4b9301: Arsenal of Soviet origin supplemented by Russian and Chinese equipment. Border security and counterterrorism doctrine.
text.ke2f628c1: Vatican City is the smallest state in the world, enclosed within Rome. Its security is provided by the Pontifical Swiss Guard and the Vatican Gendarmerie. It has no military force.
text.kfb27aa64: No armed forces: Swiss Guard and gendarmerie.
text.k4e40f9ee: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an archipelago in the Lesser Antilles. It has no army; its police provides security. Its defense falls under the Eastern Caribbean regional security system.
text.kb65d418e: Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves and borders the Caribbean Sea. In January 2026, a US military operation captured President Nicolás Maduro without toppling the government, now led by Delcy Rodríguez. Its armed forces, equipped with Russian materiel, remain largely intact.
text.ka95e7122: Mostly Russian (Su-30MK2V, T-72, S-300VM, Igla-S) and Chinese arsenal. Doctrine of popular defense and prolonged resistance.
text.k92ea729f: A long coastal country on the South China Sea, Vietnam claims the Paracel and Spratly Islands, also claimed by China. It has a large, battle-hardened army, heir to the wars of the 20th century. It is gradually modernizing its navy and coastal defenses.
text.k8ef7a863: Mostly Russian and Soviet arsenal (Su-30, T-90, Kilo submarines, Bastion missiles). Doctrine of territorial defense and area denial in the South China Sea.
text.k8d0278d6: Vanuatu is a Melanesian archipelago in the South Pacific. Its mobile force is very small. The archipelago has more than 80 islands.
text.k5d0f6916: Samoa is a Polynesian island state in the South Pacific. It has no army. Its defense relies on a friendship treaty with New Zealand.
text.k70317ee1: Kosovo is a landlocked Balkan territory whose independence, declared in 2008, is not recognized by all states. Its Security Force is being transformed into an army. A NATO force remains deployed there.
text.k0148a49e: Light forces under construction, equipped with Turkish vehicles and drones. Territorial security doctrine.
text.k32dcff56: Yemen occupies the southwestern tip of the Arabian Peninsula and borders the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key passage to the Red Sea. Since 2014 the country has been divided between the recognized government and the Houthi movement, which controls Sanaa and, since September 2026, both Yemeni shores of the strait. The Houthis have Iranian-made missiles and drones that threaten shipping.
text.kbbff69a2: Fragmented forces with old Soviet equipment, supplemented on the Houthi side by Iranian-made ballistic and anti-ship missiles and drones. Asymmetric naval blockade doctrine.
text.k3acc3de3: South Africa occupies the southern tip of the continent, at the crossroads of the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. It has the most developed defense industry in Africa, able to produce artillery, armored vehicles and attack helicopters. Its armed forces, however, suffer from chronic underfunding that reduces equipment availability.
text.k58fb35d2: Domestic (Rooivalk, Ratel, G6) and European (Gripen, MEKO frigates, Type 209) arsenal. Territorial defense and peacekeeping doctrine.
text.k3ed41a99: Zambia is a copper-rich landlocked country in southern Africa. Its armed forces are modest and equipped with Chinese materiel. It takes part in peacekeeping operations.
text.k984b7ae6: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa. Its army plays a central political role and has old Chinese equipment. Its forces have intervened in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Mozambique.
text.k463a2c37: Light arsenal of Chinese origin. Internal security doctrine.
